utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber would first like to give a decision on the motion asking for protective measures for the Witnesses W and Y. The motion is granted and a written decision will follow soon. Then, as far as the schedule for today is concerned, we are sitting a bit longer as usual. We will sit until 3.30 this afternoon. That means that we have before the first break, one hour and a half, we will then have after the break one and three-quarters of an hour and then after a relatively short lunch break, we will have another session of one hour and three-quarters of an hour so that we regain the time we lost last Friday. In order to avoid any confusion, the lunch break will be one hour and I would like to thank the interpreters very much for their flexibility and their cooperation. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I asked you last Friday whether the Defence was ready to start the cross-examination. May I now ask you whether the Defence is ready to continue the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President. But I would like to say just before, I have a point to raise and the point is the following: It may happen, as far as this witness is concerned, that we wanted to ask some questions in relation to some exhibits. And with regard to this, I would like to know if Mr. Mundis could let me know what was the answer that he may give me regarding the question of the grattage or the manipulation of documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, as you will recall, on Thursday you asked Mr. Stamp to produce a written report by today. My understanding is that that report will be done by the conclusion of today. Barring that, Mr. Ierace, will be taking the next witness and will be prepared to address any outstanding questions with respect to that written report

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. Mundis, for your information. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, Mr. President, very simply, it is what I said before, every time when there are important witnesses who knew about important facts, almost every time we fail to receive answers that we asked for. I can just stress this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you for your observation, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Apart from this issue, would the Defence be ready to continue the cross-examination of Mr. Thomas?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Continue, certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please escort Mr. Thomas into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in order to gain time, perhaps we could just have the map on the ELMO on the screen, it would be useful for later --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, if you would assist in putting the map already on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Thomas. Thank you for coming back after the weekend. May I remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration that you gave at the beginning of your testimony. We interrupted your cross-examination last Friday and it will now be continue. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you, Mr. President. Cross-examined by Mr. Piletta-Zanin: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, witness.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wanted us to look at the last exhibit that we looked at so we that continue with the cross-examination. I believe that was Exhibit number 115. Witness, just for the sake of clarity, I wanted you to read from this document the outgoing rounds from Sarajevo, please.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the outgoing fire observed from the Presidency positions?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this document which was before my time, it appears that there were 12 mortar fires -- 12 mortar rounds fired outgoing, that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And I would be grateful if you could read the incoming rounds from the Serb side.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document, again I remind the Court, which was before my time indicates that 12 artillery rounds were observed incoming.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there something else?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is nothing else incoming.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness is there a difference between these two originating sides and the side that was receiving the rounds?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not sure I understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there a difference between the number of rounds between the outgoing and the incoming rounds?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which side are you talking about? The Serb side or the Bosnian side? Is there a --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I am talking about the two sides that you just spoke of.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I reported what was outgoing fire from the Serb position and I reported outgoing fire from the Presidency positions or what, as I knew them, the Bosnian position, and they were exactly the same in that particular day. That was the outgoing fire. You haven't asked me a question about the incoming yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That could be contested because I read on page 4, line 4, the question: "Thank you very much. I would be grateful if you could read the incoming rounds from the Serb side?"

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise. My mistake. The incoming fire from the -- from -- it just says incoming fire observed on the Bosnian controlled areas. It doesn't specify that it actually came from the Serbs. But the incoming four artillery rounds and 32 mortar rounds. My apologies. I misunderstood

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Witness is there a difference between the rounds that were outgoing from Sarajevo and the rounds that were incoming on the outside of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a difference, as reported --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Again, I apologise, but in order to gain time we have to restrict ourselves just to the questions and the answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, I would like the witness to be shown a second document with the assistance of Mr. Usher, that would be document D116. If Mr. President will allow it. Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you have before you the document D116, do you?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please look at it under item 2B.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please read what you can see under item 2B.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 2B prepared in this December 1992 report indicates that five mortar rounds were observed outgoing from Presidency, what I would call Bosnian positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I would be grateful for the transcript that you read the entire sentence, please. Witness, sir, could you read item 3B.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This indicates the following --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, yes, go on.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The following incoming fire was observed on Serb controlled areas, artillery 3, mortar 103, tank, nil.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Since you read 3A, I would now ask you to read 2A, please.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: 2A, the following outgoing fire was observed from Presidency or what I would call Bosnian positions and what it says is "artillery, nil."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, would you agree with me to say that there is a serious difference between these two observation points?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't agree that there was a serious difference.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you for your answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if you ask whether there is any serious difference, mathematical differences as far as I understand, which does not appear in the transcript, the witness should be allowed to explain if he has an explanation for that difference. Just establishing that the numbers are not the same might be of importance, but if the witness wants to add something, he is allowed to do something.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I explained earlier, the observation posts located on the inside of the city were created to provide observation of the city and the areas shelled. They were not in a position to see the Bosnian gun positions, nor were we kept informed of either the Bosnian or Serb gun positions. So, we were not in a good position to see what was fired from inside the city. On the other hand, our locations on the Bosnian Serb side had been selected primarily to monitor outgoing artillery rounds fired by the Bosnian Serbs. So I would expect in normal professional practice, that we would hear and see more on the Bosnian Serb side than we would hear or see from within the city. Also, this is only the military observer part. It does not cater for rounds reported by the other UN military forces. Also, there was a serious discrepancy in the numbers of weapons, both within the city and in comparison to those outside.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That goes beyond the observations of this report. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Now, with the assistance of Mr. Usher, I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 117, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, do you see this document before you?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I now see document 117, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you keep on eye on what are Article 70 documents because we might not always know and please indicate if we will have to go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I will do so, Mr. President, and raise the same concerns that I raised on Friday with respect to the scope of how much we will be able to do in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Please keep a close eye on it and indicate when you think it cannot be done any more in open session. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, do you see item 2A?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I would like to ask you to read the first two paragraphs, even the first three paragraphs of item 2A, please. Could you do that? Just a moment. Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am sorry. Mr. Mundis

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: My learned colleague has asked the witness to read 75 per cent of this document and I would ask that that be done in closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I was never going to ask for 75 per cent to be read --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...or 21. If this is an Article 70 document, then if we are reading more than just a few numbers, but parts of a paragraph, then we should turn into closed session. Could we please turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we are in open session again. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Mundis. This escaped my attention and I should have been able to see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, we just heard your answer which I am going to repeat for technical reasons according to which you said "that certainly there were people in civilian clothes on the trenches, in the trenches, in order to dig them." That is what I understood from your answer. I am going to ask you another question, please, which is the following: Do you know if the army of Sarajevo organised raids in the streets picking people up, yes, in order to round people up and forcibly take them to the location of the trenches?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I must correct your understanding. There were people in civilian clothes digging in the trenches, but now to answer your second question, no, I am not aware of --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Witness. Witness, with the assistance of the usher I would like to draw you to Exhibit 118.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, have you got this two-page document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, the same exercise as before. I will do it for you, to make it quicker. Could you confirm that under item 2 "that is the outgoing fire position observed from Papa positions. We have nothing in terms of tanks, mortars, multiple rocket launchers or AAAs." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would agree with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. As regards item 3 which has to do with incoming fire, is it true that we can see that there were 18 mortar shots on the Lima side, the Bosnian Serbian side?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what this report before my time indicates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now we shall move on to another document with the assistance of the usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to have D119 given to the witness and with the assistance of Madam Registrar, I would like to have P1753 taken out again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you the two documents in front of you, Witness?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, is number 119, is it dated October 18th 1993?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, is Exhibit 1753 --

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- does it also relate to the period of 18th of October, the date 1993, 18th October 1993?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It covers the time from 1800 hours, 17 October, the night or through the night of 17 October to 1800 hours on 18 October. So the time frames by this are not the -- exactly the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The time frames are not exactly the same but the dates seem to correspond to each other. Witness, would you kindly read what we find in brackets in 1753, that is to say, the end of the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: "My military observers reported that 67 mixed artillery rounds and are tank rounds and mortar rounds fell on the Bosnian side today, that is within the reporting period of --"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, kindly read what you have in the last sentence of paragraph A of Exhibit 119. Of the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I take it you are assuming to military activity and you are talking about "UNPROFOR recorded 40 mortar and artillery shells in the Zuc area and the source is a newspaper."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Quite. Now, please read the line below just below.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: "It says on the --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Below. Above, sorry.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you give me the first word?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. It is the second line of the first paragraph. And it begins by "19," I think.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: "19 shells reportedly hit the city over night and BH forces returned a smaller number of rounds."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. Would there be any contradictions between the two exhibits?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I can't answer that with a "yes" or "no." It requires an explanation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain briefly, please do?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military observer reports cover from 1800 hours on 17 October to 1800 hours on 18 October. This report which appears to have been prepared or submitted by a newspaper, it -- I have no idea what time they are talking about on 18 October. They may have been talking from the first time they got up in the morning until when the sun went down or maybe they are talking about from 000 hours on the 18th to 000 hours -- 2400 hours --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I am stopping you now. Do you know what document 119 corresponds to?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have never seen this kind of document before?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have seen many documents similar to this before and I see at the top -- I can't understand from the heading which particular documents it is from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you cannot tell us, Witness, to the best of your knowledge, whether this document was prepared on the basis of what you call "a sitrep, a shootrep, increp"?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Military -- my military observer reports may very well have contributed to this. On the other hand, they may not. I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, with the assistance of the usher, Mr. President, I would like the witness to be provided with Exhibit 120 which is now here. With the assistance of this madam secretary, I would like to have the witness be given Exhibit 1824 -- 1884, sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have both documents before you?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With the same observations of a few minutes ago, we are dealing with November 29, 1993, in both cases.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are not exactly the same time frame.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, by looking at these documents, let us focus on -- I will find it immediately. Paragraph 3 of item A, military activity, could you please read it out.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: 3 from which report?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just said A, military activity of document 120.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Starting with description of damage?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Sarajevo lost a good proportion of its electricity due to shelling damage to the electricity generating station in Jablanica, 40 miles to the west of the city, source United Press International."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that we have the sources. Are they -- have they been confirmed by the observers, first question? Were they confirmed by the observers, first question? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you asking us to confirm about an electrical generating station that is 40 miles?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I am asking you about that in this document, and please bear in mind that it is an official document that was established on the basis of observations made in Sarajevo. When we see United Press International as a source, now, the military observers on the ground, would they go and verify those sources or not?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't act on the reports of the United Press International. We acted on our own orders and damages that we observed or shelling that we observed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, if I see a reference like United Press International in an official document, can I then say that the observers did not verify it?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no way of knowing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now please look at document 1884.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, 1884 was tendered under seal so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have to go back --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we are in open session again. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Now we shall move on to another series of questions and if you allow me to have document D121 delivered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you should have before you a document of four pages; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recognise this type of document, sir?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, is it true to say that this is a list of the wounded and the missing for the months that I mentioned?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it isn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, what is this?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a list of the sniper casualties. And as you can see from the document, it also includes some UN casualties such as date March 06, one French soldier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. I forgot to mention that these were wounded or disappeared because of sniping, but we agree on that, that we are speaking about the same thing. Now, I would like --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would simply object to the categorization as "disappeared". I think from the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, whether you meant to say that they faded away from this life or that you intended to say that they were not found again.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, that is not missing in action. These are people who died. This is the usual form. I didn't pick up the interpretation because I thought it was a minor point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. When you are talking about those who disappeared, you mean those who died.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed to answer the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the objection is opposed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the objection is denied or whether I understood it as a clarification is up for the Chamber to decide.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, on the items 010205 to 07, you could see the end of the first column regarding the losses, you have asterisks that I mentioned. When we are referring to the legend which is a footnote at the bottom of the page, we can see that other data is not accessible, is not available. But in this column, sir, we only have two things. We have the wounded that are mentioned by a "WS" wounded and those who died, who were killed, that is indicated by letter "K" for killed. Now, why is it not possible to find out if a person was wounded or if it was dead? Because there are no other -- not many other possibilities. Someone was either wounded or killed, but there is no third possibility that is available. Could you perhaps clarify this for us?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. This report would have been prepared by somebody at the site of the sniper incident. Of course, if they are taken off as wounded, they may later die. So what -- to determine the exact casualties for the day, it would be necessary to look at our summary, because we checked the morgue at night. This is only a summary of the sniping incident. Also, you will see that most of those further details unable to occur at the beginning when we just started this procedure. After the teams became more used to what was required -- and you will find that they generally found out what happened to the casualties later. So initially they weren't aware that we should be tracking what happened to the casualty, whether he was -- stayed wounded or whether he, in fact, died in the hospital. But as we got more proficient in preparing this data, then you will see there is only a few cases in the following months where we have further details unavailable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you for the explanation. We can see, for instance, under item 11, there is a term, "unknown" regarding the location of the incident. What could you tell us on this subject, sir?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This would be a body that we found, that we were investigating, where we didn't find the body at the site of where the killing took place or the wounding took place. This would be somebody that was obviously wounded by small-arms fire, presumably by a sniper, and the exact location at the time was not known. And again --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you, sir. Now, Witness, I would like to ask you a series of questions regarding the locating of these incidents. We have the figures here which were done in tables. Are you familiar with these figures?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: These -- are you talking about the grid references? Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: With this --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With the figures themselves.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They are map references.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Could you tell us for item 01, to which area does the first figure correspond 9388 -- 881643?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would require looking it up on a map, and this map you provided me doesn't have the same grid that these figures would be in. However, this would be -- would allow us to relate to the operational map that we had in the headquarters which we would then use to brief people on where the sniper activity occurred.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I simply asked you a question, to see if you were familiar with these figures, if you are able to locate them in space without your premarked map. But could you tell us to which areas do these figures correspond to or not?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The map you have given me is in fact a city map and doesn't even have grid lines at the top. It has letters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't answer without my own map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the question was whether you could relate these numbers to specific places without using a map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, on this document we can see on several occasions abbreviation, "BSA." Could you confirm what that is?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: BSA was the short term for Bosnian Serb army. So, in fact, on the 1st of March the casualty that day was a Bosnian Serb army soldier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is, either shot at, wounded or killed by a sniper from the so-called BH army?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We assume that he was shot by a sniper from the BH army. We have the same rumours about the Bosnian Serb army as we have about the Bosnian army, that sometimes they shot their own people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I did not ask the question in relation to sniper. So there were rumours, according to you, according to which there were Muslim snipers that were sniping their own people?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were rumours that people were killed by people on their own side for other reasons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would those be political reasons, sir?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In some cases it was suspected, and other cases, criminal activity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer, Witness. When you spoke of political reasons, would it be perhaps to stir the media or was it perhaps to increase the figures for political reasons?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly that would be a political reason to do this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is, at the same time there would be more victims, increasing the numbers of victims, and also attracting the compassion of the media; is that how I am to understand your answer?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be true, although you will see on the 9th of March most casualties were BSA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it indeed. Witness, to come back to the document, there is one thing that I am surprised by and this is the abbreviation "FRE." Do you know what it corresponds to?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That corresponds to French.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is a French soldier?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I said before when you asked me about this document, this is a summary of sniping. We tried to identify the casualties, whether from either side or from the UN forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Sir, I would like to go back to the question of sniping, but just before that, I have a question for the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, looking at the -- considering the time table, are we going to stop at quarter past or half past?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We started at 9.00, so we will have our first break at half past 10.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, to go back to the sniping, and you spoke of these political considerations, do you know, as far as you know, these sniping activities were they increasing either when the media was particularly present or when political, specific political events were going on in Sarajevo, for instance, arrival of important political figures?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know of at least one instance where there was a sniping incident which occurred for which there was no reason except that CNN was passing by within a certain time while the casualty would still be there. And this occurred in June. But I can't be sure --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, thank you, Witness, for the relative precision of your answer. Could you tell us if not when, then where did this happen?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This happened at the junction of the road from the airport and the road that leads into Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Sir, is it true, and I believe that you indicated it, that the balance, so to speak, the balance of victims was not always, let's use the word "correct," when we are talking about the facts when the Bosnian Serb army was a lot more unwilling to communicate its number of wounded and killed soldiers?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am assuming that you are referring to the fact that we didn't -- the UN did not know all the Bosnian Serb casualties. Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Sir, as an officer of the armoured force you would know that there would be a factory needed to manufacture weapons in Sarajevo. Now, I am going to go back for the -- I am going to go back for the English interpretation. Do you know about the existence of a factory -- factories, thank you, factories that were able to manufacture weapons or equipment that would be useful or used by snipers? Do you know of such facilities in the city?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nor do I think they were needed. There was storage of enough munitions before the war to provide most of the ammunition and special equipment needed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness when you say that you don't know it, do you exclude the possible presence of factories in the city?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would -- we didn't suspect a factory in the city because it didn't make military sense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was, Mr. Thomas, whether you could exclude the presence of such factories?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Anything was possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. Sir, does the name of a factory, called Zrak, does it mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know, Witness, that optical instruments that were used for sniping rifles were manufactured by the Zrak factory?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Sir, you spoke earlier of ammunition depos. What do you know about these ammunition depos? Where were they, what were their names, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the exact location of ammunition depos. I do know that in my preparatory briefing in Canada, we were advised that there was enough ammunition in the stocks of the Yugoslav home Defence forces for this war to be carried on for 40 years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, when you use the expression in English "the Yugoslav home defence forces," are you referring to what was known as the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It -- yes. It is the concept that there was a manoeuvre army which would manoeuvre around the Yugoslavs who defended their own home locality after they had served their conscript time. To make this possible on the Swiss model which I am sure you are familiar with, there was a great series of depos, ammunition storage at the very local level because the concept rests on the idea that locally trained people can respond to an emergency and defend their own locality without depending on support from outside. This in turn meant that large quantities of small arms ammunition and artillery ammunition for the calibres that we are talking about, 120 millimetre, and even guns and field pieces, would be able in especially an urban area like Sarajevo, which would be a key part of such a concept, because motorised forces would bypass Sarajevo if it was strongly defended.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer, sir. And I would like to say that you are extremely well-informed in any case about the Swiss system, as well as the Yugoslav system. When you spoke of the concept of defence, and that is the first part of your answer, is it true that this concept of defence would implicate the obligation for any man of military age to bear arms to defend his territory, whatever the definition of the territory is, with the weapons, if he has any?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of the exact provisions. It was my understanding that those that completed military training, that is, done their service with the JNA, would then be required to be part of some form of home defence unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, regarding the weapon depos, we have certain testimony that indicated that these weapons were partly preserved with large public companies of ex-Yugoslavia. Could you confirm this information?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not sure I understand the question. You say --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will repeat it, gladly. According to some testimonies it seems that the weapons that we spoke of were practically preserved by public companies, enterprises, of the former Yugoslavia. Could you confirm this fact?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Am I to understand that you are saying that some public companies assisted in the storage and preservation of these weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is what we learned from a testimony, yes, that is correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: By the time of my tour there, the public companies really weren't operating in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I know that but you spoke of your briefing in Canada before that. And were you spoken about this during the briefing, were you told about this?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were told that there were storage sites everywhere in the former Yugoslavia and it was a question of each locality had its own storage sites. At that time I didn't pay particular attention to Sarajevo because I didn't know I was going to go there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that each locality, does that mean that every municipality in fact would have that?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my understanding, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, is it true that there were several municipalities in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that would be the case. And this munitions would be stored very carefully because they must be preserved against surprise attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, sir, is it true to say that the troops known as government forces or Muslim forces had at their disposal during the time frame we are talking about, important quantities of weapons and ammunitions?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No it isn't clear because we do not know how much ammunition and stores were taken by the JNA when they evacuated Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, talking about ammunition, do you know of an existence of a tunnel which was linking the interior of the city and the outside of the city, the famous Dobrinja Butmir tunnel?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Witness, do you know if this tunnel was used for the needs of bringing in supplies for the military?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that today?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you know if there were any other systems in place that were used to smuggle in to bring in on the sly, weapons into Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No other specific areas. We suspected smuggling occurred wherever they were running people on the Bosnian Serb side to permit this to take place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, are you, and that is probably the last question before the break or did you know about the operation that was known at the time as "operation oxygen"?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, did you hear or did you know about an operation which consisted of delivering to one of the sides in the conflict explosives or gunpowder in oxygen bottles which were supposedly for medical use?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I believe the time has come for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will adjourn until 11.00. May I remind you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you have approximately 50 minutes left. You have approximately 50 minutes left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. With the assistance of the usher, I would like to give the witness document 123, 123.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, before you receive the document, on the basis of the map you have in front of you, could you tell us if you recognise the --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The next number Mr. Piletta-Zanin, is 122.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is very generous. On the part of the Defence, 122 has disappeared. It will come at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, on the map that you have to your right, can you find and indicate where this Sharpstone zone is located? Witness?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think I can give a general idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you kindly, with the assistance of the usher, to put the map on the screen so that we can see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...Mr. Thomas, if you put it on the machine on the right-hand side of you, we can follow whatever you...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We are seeing -- it is very hard to see, because the highest feature is here, but you have got dominating --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you very much. For the transcript, the witness pointed to the 7 woods area or 7 forests area, which we can see in square "L." It is on the upper part of the map. Thank you, Witness. Could you kindly circle the zone. Could you draw a circle around it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please do that with a black --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, thank you.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Do you know whether in that zone there were trenches limiting the two warring factions? Was it there in that zone?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were trenches that I observed that on the Bosnian Serb area side of the line. I don't recall seeing the Bosnian positions in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you then try to find the trenches in that zone?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This map is too generalized. I need a topographical map. I can't show you on this map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, kindly take document 123 which you have before you. Please tell us if you recognise that kind of document? I expect you do.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise this type of document, however --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Still what we are interested in is page 2, please. And I would kindly ask you to read item 6A, first sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object to this document on two grounds. The first ground being that it is outside the indictment period and I would also ask in light of the fact that this is a Rule 70 document, that depending on the number of questions that Mr. Piletta-Zanin has, that we go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but before doing so, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, when the witness said that this was not within his period of time, the period of time he spent in Sarajevo, you responded by saying "I am mainly interested in page 2" which covers the same time period, as far as I can see. Was it anything specific because we can't expect the witness to tell us anything about the period, but if it is just about logics or the type of document, that might be different. But then we will have to turn into closed session first.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To gain time, Mr. President, I will renounce to this document and I will then hand out document 124.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 123 is withdrawn and will not be tendered. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that later 122 will come up. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It will arrive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the document just withdrawn will now be replaced then by the new one prenumbered 124, which will now be 123.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thought that the documents remained numbered as they were. But then we will change all the numbers. All right. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you have in front of you a document which comes from the conference on the former Yugoslavia. We are dealing with item 2, Sarajevo, and it focuses on Grbavica and Zuc. Can you confirm that these two localities were frequently fighting zones?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Witness, could you please turn to page 2 of the document, item 10, no fly zone. Have you that page in front of you?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you confirm, if you know, what was the number of UN flights, approximately, which landed and departed from Sarajevo daily?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea. UNHCR representative would be a better source of this information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Witness, now I would like to move to document 124, with the assistance of the usher. It is a document addressed to Lord Owen and Mr. Stoltenberg. Witness, as regards to item 2, Sarajevo, could you confirm, "yes" or "no," whether Rajlovac, Zuc and Hum were also places where combat fighting were very intense?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you confirm that Rajlovac is in the town of Sarajevo proper?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I considered it a suburb myself, but it is in the area of Sarajevo, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, when fighting would take place in Rajlovac, were there in the technical considerations on the basis of which the front and the back zone were determined, could you perhaps tell us how far behind, how deep, was the back zone? Was it in the direction of Rajlovac, a few hundreds of metres, a kilometre, as you indicated, or perhaps more?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is easiest if I describe this on the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, begin by describing it on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Usher, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas, we noticed that you made some markings on documents where you were not requested to mark them. Would you please not do that because then we might have some difficulties.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry, Mr. Chairman, I was just marking to make sure I had captured the area that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The documents shown to you, unless specifically asked for, should be leaving your desk in the same condition as when they arrived at your desk.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry. Basically the front line in the Rajlovac area we considered this road almost as no-man's land with the Bosnian Serb positions on this side and the Bosnian forces on this side. And there was a gap of no-man's land because the Bosnian positions were on the higher ground. So there was an area here where these forces at this end of the Bosnian position in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. confronting Rajlovac, would have in fact have to been resupplied probably from the Zuc area. And closer to the city proper where there was trenches lines here which then started to move out towards the Stup area, you would find that they could in fact have some supplies and replacements in this area here. In this area here, there is a stretch area here where these houses are shown, was basically a no-man's land where these buildings were all destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So we understand that there was a no-man's land. Was there a safety security zone behind that zone?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the Serb side, in fact, they had depth to this position. So their lines would go along here and I can't remember exactly where they cut into the Stup, but they had some depth. The Bosnians are -- were in what we call a forward position on a slope here. So as they came off these spurs on the mountain they were on the forward slope. So I suspect, and we didn't see it, that they had to resupply at night. In this area here of course, the built-up area allowed some cover for movement during the day. And this was heavy. This railway line here had trenches up to the railway line. The railway line posed a problem for both sides because of its embankment and there assaulting troops would have to go up, expose themselves, and then come down to attack. So the approach was to tunnel through it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Witness, you have just said that the Bosnia troops were on higher ground from the two heights that you have just shown us on the map. Could they dominate the town; "yes" or "no"?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could they dominate the Rajlovac sector, yes; could they dominate Sarajevo, no, way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, now we will move to something else, that is Exhibit 22 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the sake of the transcript, the witness has pointed at various places, but they are all within the area covered by B-1 up to D-4.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since we are dealing with the map now, with the assistance of the usher, could you move the map to the left so we could see the sector of the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you assist Mr. Thomas in moving the map so that we can see the Old City.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There, we have found it. Witness, given your very accurate knowledge of the area, could you carefully listen to my question and try to answer very precisely because this has to be put on the transcript and that is why I am asking you to act in that way. To the west -- to the south of what we can see here and now, the lower part, were there trenches or fortifications in the lower part of the picture we can see now? And for the transcript, I would like to say that this square 4, number 4, G, M, L and so forth -- K, M, L up to square 4, did you understand my question, Witness?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not sure that I understand exactly the question or where you want me to put --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that zone that you are looking at now were there front lines?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you show them to us using the pointer?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I couldn't. This map doesn't have the kind of detail I need. It is too large a scale for something as precise as trenches.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you do it in a general way?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because it is misleading.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Witness these front lines, are they located in the area of the square that we can see now? I think it is number 4 on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, would you please refer precisely to the square because --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall go back to it. I asked for our city plan just to make things clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, were there in that zone which corresponds to the line of the square 4 to the south, south of the Vitesak [phoen] River, were there any lines or a front line --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He is pointing at K-4. Is that to the square you referred to or do you want to refer to J, K, L and/or M?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] J, K, L, M from line 4

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas, from J-4 up to M-4.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is asking me to place the line incorrectly because the only positions that I saw for sure, were the Serb positions along the Pale road in the area that I am tracing now which are actually in the 5 square. They were there facing Bosnian positions. So in fact, in some areas, the lines were actually in the 5 squares.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, let us summarise for the transcript. The lines indicated by the witness are in zone 5 of the square between lines K and L, north of the Lukavica road. Is that correct, Witness?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this map is too imprecise to show exactly where the lines --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We know that. But on the basis of what you have shown, I think this is what -- that it is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas, if you would point as precisely as possible to the trenches as you could have observed them, then we will be able to translate it into transcript language.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, let him first point.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Somewhere along this line here and I can't be absolutely precise without my own map. Their Serb positions were just to the north of the Pale road. And when I stopped at some of the Serb positions, I could see through the trees, I could definitely pick out the Bosnian trench line as well. Serbs in this case were on the higher ground defending the Pale road and the Bosnians would have to attack uphill. And they had reached this point in October almost to the Pale road. They were trying to cut it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness was pointing at the east-west road that goes through K-5. And L-5 starting approximately where in small letters it says "Sumarska" going down to the south-east up to where L-5 goes into M-5 and he indicated just north of this road. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in relation to that zone could you tell us what the depth of the back zone, rear zone?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I couldn't. However, my assessment would be that it would be under cover and there was wooded cover partway up the hill as you can see from this map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. What do you know about the 10th Hill Brigade? Was it located there?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be sure of its exact location. It was disbanded within a month after my arrival and presumably this was done because of its poor combat efficiency. So in fact, I can't be sure of who actually was doing the fighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether a certain Caco was in charge of that brigade?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This person was reported to be in charge. I never met him. He was removed before they took me to that headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether that person was a criminal who was searched for by his own people?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand the Bosnian government dealt with him as a criminal. The Bosnian government themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, Mr. President, I would like to have Exhibit 122 submitted, just to be in line with the chronology, with the assistance of the usher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you see the top right of the document where there were buildings and whose roofs are somewhat destroyed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is this a comprehensive document?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I don't believe so, Mr. President, based on the lack of an "R" number on the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I was waiting for my answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you see in the top right corner -- Witness, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see in the top right corner of this document, buildings that are destroyed?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The buildings that I can identify destroyed are more in the centre. They are missing their roofs. The one at the top right-hand corner I can hardly seen it in the photograph that I have been asked to examine. I can clearly see the ones in the centre, the roof has been partially destroyed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can't you see that the other buildings are also destroyed or seem also destroyed?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ones in the centre, yes, I can confirm that they seem destroyed, at least two of them do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. The buildings that you see to your right, do they seem to you to be civilian buildings and I am talking about the buildings you can see in the top right corner?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they appear to be civilian buildings.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. These buildings that they can be described as civilian, would it be reported as having been shelled as civilian buildings, if these are civilian buildings?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only if we observe the fall of shot on those particular buildings and obviously they must have been hit, because they are in fact -- the buildings have been partially destroyed. But to determine whether we would have reported that or not it would have to be in context. I don't know where the trenches are in relation to these buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, in relation to the civilian buildings, can you see straight in the centre of the photograph, a little to the left of the PR target, air target, can you see a dark mark, a black mark? It is a dark mark which would correspond to a trench.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe. I can't determine it from the photograph I have --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. If I tell you that, could you make out what is written at the bottom of the document?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says "a plan, incline, enters to a tunnel" and then it says --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you understand that?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I still don't know where this is from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is this a document from Sarajevo or from where is it in relation to anything else?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have never seen such a document?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not like this, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is just I may have seen documents, area photographs of Sarajevo but this one can can't be sure what context it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, for the transcript, this is simply entrance to the Butmir tunnel with the civilian buildings around, that were unfortunately hit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution objects to the extent that Mr. Piletta-Zanin seems to be testifying. The witness has said he has no idea where this is. We would object to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The objection is sustained. The witness has not testified on it and everyone who can read sees that the words "entrance to the tunnel" is on the photograph. Whether it is a picture of the entrance of the tunnel, we do not know. We just know that it is written on it. So it is not just a matter of the transcript, but if you say for the transcript, I am referring to a photograph which bears as text on it "the entrance of the tunnel." But you are asking the witness a lot of questions about a map he says he doesn't know. That is not what we usually do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps, Mr. President, but the aim of the questions with the view of this photograph is to see to which extent it is difficult to determine whether that is a civilian building or not. And the answer that the witness gave that I was interested in was that these were civilian buildings. They are undoubtedly civilian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's just then look very precisely to his testimony, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. The question was whether these buildings can be described as civilian, would it be reported as having been shelled as civilian buildings? So it is rather hypothetical. I do not see that the witness testified that these were civilian buildings. It just said that as far as he could see from the photograph, that they appear to be civilian buildings. It looks as if that is the same to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is the same thing. Because, Mr. President, when the observers say that civilian areas were hit, we say "it appears that" and that is exactly the same thing. This is what I wanted to demonstrate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it has got nothing to do with the tunnel or does it have to do anything with the tunnel?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it does. This has to do with the tunnel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...that this is a picture which indicates where a tunnel is and the witness has testified that he does not know unless there is --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...that this would be a picture on which a tunnel is visible or indicated that there was a tunnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, clearly the text on Defence Exhibit 122 indicates that, but again, Prosecution view is there is no proper foundation in light of the fact that the witness has said he doesn't know what this photograph is of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Whether it is true or not, the witness doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Exactly, Mr. President. I don't know if there was an ERN number under the Defence Exhibit sticker. Other than that, I am at a loss as to where this document came from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if you have any additional questions, please keep in mind what we -- what the Chamber just --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have any questions regarding this document, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I would like to have the witness shown with the assistance of Mr. Usher a written statement taken on the 16th, 17th and 18th of November, 1999, I believe, and I would like to ask the witness if he recognises his signature and the document.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, sir, I would be grateful if you could tell me on page 644 --

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- 5th paragraph, 4th paragraph, could you please read what comes under paragraph 4, please?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one that starts with "Galic"? "Galic, Sarajevo Romanija Corps, BSA Commander met him once before February 1994 --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please slow down a bit, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry. And then later --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please continue, Witness, the transcript will follow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "And then later in the context of the negotiations for the total exclusion zone. Also, during the same time, I accompanied General Soubirou and Galic to Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, we can stop here. Thank you very much. Now, Witness, thank you for reading this. And the question is the following: General Galic was therefore active, whatever the importance of the activity, but he was active as to implementing the ceasefire from the beginning of 1994; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would say so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Sir, I would be grateful if you could go on to the following page, please. And to read for us the second paragraph that is roughly in the middle starting with the sentence, "I also saw a collection" and so on? Did you find it?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is this page 645?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's correct. Second paragraph in the middle, exactly line 6.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I will read it. " Also saw a collection of very well equipped Bosnian troops, French equipment prior to an attack in Grbavica. In the case of Grbavica, it appeared to be a very-well coordinated attack making good use of the Bosnian asset infantry to combat the Serb asset artillery and tanks. In a location --" I seem have given some problem there. "In a location which suited the Bosnian asset best."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. Now sir, page 647, please. First paragraph. And we would start by line 6 which starts with "I did succeed in entering one location."

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I did succeed in entering one location," referring to my visit to sniper locations, "which --"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't have to add anything. Just read, please.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Which was in a school in Dobrinja from which the BH covered the road to BSA Corps headquarters at Lukavica. It was directly opposite a church from which the Serbs had snipers firing into Dobrinja. When I entered the Bosnian location, I found police officers who appeared very professional and had good equipment. It is possible that they were trained as part of an anti-terrorist squad for the 1984 Olympics."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You indicated earlier, but that was my question which was to come. Witness, when you visited this school it was in relation to a kind of tour that you did with relation to the snipers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't -- I don't like the word "tour." It was in response to reported violations from the Serb side we attempted to visit the source of sniping on the Bosnian side. It was an investigation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Do you remember the name of the school?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't remember the name of the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Were there other schools?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't even recall the exact -- the exact situation of the building. I was more interested in what was inside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, sir, do you know the name of Kazani? Does this mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you know about the existence of Tarcin? Does this mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Tarcin or --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tarcin, that is T-a-r-c-i-n.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have to clarify whether that is a person or a location.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is a location.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't clear on your pronunciation, but you are talking about a town that is outside the Sector Sarajevo boundaries, but wasn't -- but which was involved, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that is it. I am sorry about my pronunciation, sir. I will try and do better in the future. But do you know whether there was a detention camp there?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many people and who was -- whose camp was it?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only know the details on periphery because I provided a team of military observers to assist in the investigation. So I can provide the Court with what details I know and recall after this time or you can probably have access to UN documents which have more detail.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But as far as you know, was this a camp for Serb prisoners?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a camp for Serb prisoners who generally appeared to be from the town of Hadzici and this was the excuse used for taking UN people hostage in Hadzici in the end of March, 1994. Women surrounded a UN convoy there and wanted to hold the convoy until their men folk were released from this detention centre on the Bosnian side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, these men were not prisoners of war? Not prisoners of war, they were not prisoners?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
