utterances.text: I didn't see the camp. Neither side respected the prisoner of war because it is a political question of whether there was a war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There seems to be some misunderstanding as to the "prisoner". Mr. Piletta-Zanin is asking you whether these were prisoners, not prisoners of war, but prisoners under normal law.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. It was my understanding they were being treated as prisoners of war in the sense that the Red Cross, I think, visited them, as well as UNHCR. So as such -- I mean, there were lots of people held because of the fighting and there was a question of the status of these people because it was not seen as a legitimate case of war in the sense that the Republic of Srpska was not a legal entity. So I think we used the word "detainee" to avoid attaching the word "prisoner of war" when in some circles it was not agreed that this was in fact a war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, in other words, these people were detained because of their ethnic origin?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't say that. They were detained because they were men of military age who could possibly engage in fighting and who would have certainly been of an age to have completed their military training in the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness I would like to go back to some parts of your statement, but first of all I would like to have the document 125 shown to you with the assistance of Mr. Usher, please, which is in relation to what we spoke of earlier; that is, in relation to the ceasefire to which General Galic cooperated a great deal. Witness, do you have this document before you?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It originated with the military observers but as a formal protest. It had to be submitted by the sectors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Colonel Sonic?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a high-quality professional?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Outstanding officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Is it true, since you certainly know this document by heart, is it true that this Colonel was complaining of a ceasefire violations on the Muslim side, by the Muslim side?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, the answer is not completely correct. As the incident took place on the boundaries on Sector Sarajevo in the Mount Igman area, on a route that we suspected to be an infiltration route for reinforcing Gorazde. It was at the extreme limits of the sector Sarajevo area which is why it was picked up by military observers and not by anybody else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer, Witness. Now on the subject of the ceasefire, could you please remind us approximately how long it lasted? Was it four months? Five months?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, obviously when the first sniper shot was fired, the ceasefire was broken we already started data collection on the 1st of March. I think that the chances of making peace were disappearing when I left in July of 1994 and they had already been shaken by the attack in Gorazde in April 1994 and the NATO air strikes and the subsequent change in the military posture of both sides.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, would you agree with me to consider that from the beginning of the debates, with regard to establishing the ceasefire until the month that I just indicated, there was more or less a decrease, a notable decrease of combats, of warring acts, whatever they were?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely. The first -- the last two weeks of February, there was almost no military action whatsoever on the front lines of either party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, therefore, if I can follow your answer, from the end of January until the end of July 1994, as you have just indicated, that was the period historically where there was an important decrease, a considerable decrease on combat activity and military activity. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the ceasefire of mid-February 1994 until I left in July, there was no artillery fire in the city. And there was --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- increasing sniper fire, as more and more it seemed before I left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, since I know that we took our time, but unfortunately, the Defence had to prepare very quickly, as you know, and the Defence would like to use a little more time and I am saying this because of necessity, if this is possible

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just confer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the Defence has until 10 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I am going to go back to the Exhibit 2170, that you were given, as well as 3506 [As interpreted] and Witness these are incidents of the 22nd of January 1994 and incidents on the 4th of February 1994. The exhibits that we saw when you were examined last week, do you remember them?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not until I see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember these two dates, the 22nd of January 1994 and the 4th of February 1994?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not particularly. I might recall them when I see the two reports.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Sir, these are incidents where six children --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I believe the English transcript said one of the documents is P3506 and it should be 3706.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, it is in relation to an incident where six children were victims of a shelling that took place on the 22nd of January and on the other hand of an incident to the south of Sarajevo where there were also victims including three children?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have the documents in front of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question that I wanted to ask you, Witness, is the following: Do you know if these incidents caused one, an investigation done by a mixed international commission, or any investigation they would have asked questions in relation to the commission or asked the General Galic's staff?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. These occurred before the ceasefire. So the mixed commission -- the joint commission which was created at the ceasefire was not in existence. These --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am sorry. I am going to interrupt you here. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. You therefore say that the international commission, the mixed joint commission, was established only after the ceasefire to which -- in which General Galic cooperated; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not sure of what mixed commission you otherwise would be talking about. Are you --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I am talking about. Precisely. There were no commissions before?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in Sector Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, no more questions on these two exhibits. You can put them aside, Witness. But I would like you to take your statements as we looked at before please. This must be page 646, again. And I would like you to read of paragraph 4 which begins with "regarding protests of attacks on civilians." Could you find it?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please read it?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Regarding protests on attacks of civilians. Prior to the February 1994 the sides were at war so it was rather difficult to protest anything. However, in the context of negotiations with all levels of the warring factions it was a constant theme that we did not want any shooting. But if there was any, they should limit their fire to people in uniform. One of the problems with this was a question of who was a soldier. Many people, including women and children, wore camouflage and then many people who were military wore civilian clothes."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness you are, therefore, indicating that civilians were wearing camouflage clothes and mistakes were technically possible?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this requires elaboration. Some of the aid that came to Sarajevo, such as from Germany, included items of winter clothing that had a military nature, such as parkas that were given to people in the city from the German army. So, yes, it could possibly be a mistake in if you were targeting individual people, however, artillery is an area weapon, and you target an area. And you usually base that --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I have to interrupt you for reasons of time saving. I am talking about sniping, you know, that we make a difference between the two things.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, Mr. President, I am going to ask that the witness be shown, and we are going to try to do it all at once, these are two statements of other people. These are statements with numbers ERN 02030107 and 020216. But I can see Mr. Mundis on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Again, Mr. President, the Prosecution would object to this witness being shown statements of other witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this witness testified to a large number of things and he spoke of this person, Caco, who was considered to be a criminal. And this person it seems was rounding people up and bringing civilians to the front line. So I believe that we are talking about relevant things and I wanted to perhaps refresh the witness's memory in relation to some facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution is not objecting on the grounds of relevance, but simply on the procedure which Mr. Piletta-Zanin intends to employ. He mentions refreshing the witness's memory in relation to some facts. He can certainly do that without showing this witness statements of other witnesses.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are just at this moment discussing a procedural issue. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, as Mr. Mundis indicated, it is not for reasons of relevance, and you may question the witness about certain events that are facts in your view, but you cannot refresh the memory of this witness by showing him a statement of any other witness. So the subject is not forbidden ground, but the technique you used. So the objection is sustained. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Witness we have a statement by another person, a man called --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, saying who gave the statement, reading the content of the statement, would be the same as showing the statement to the witness. So, therefore, I ask that -- the subject is not forbidden ground, but the technique, and you are, as a matter of fact, using, not in writing, the same technique. Would you please keep this in mind while questioning the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we have grounds to believe, Witness, that on some occasions it happens that civilians dressed in civilian clothes who were killed on or in or around the area of trenches because they found themselves there because they were forced to be there. Have you never heard any such things?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was never -- if there was any talk, it was only a rumour. Because the people that I observed on the front line, appeared to be there willingly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, if we start from the principal that this was not a rumour and that indeed there were people who were civilian and who ended up being killed in the trenches, on the trenches, I make a logical conclusion that when UN forces went to check the bodies in the mortuary, they did not know either whether such-and-such civilian had been killed in or around the trenches. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That could be the case, although everybody that we looked at in the morgue might or might not have military pieces of uniform for wear. We, for sure, did not count women and children as military.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it true that there was a brigade that also had women soldiers in their ranks?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The cases of women in the ranks were rare enough that it was noteworthy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Sir was there a 7th Brigade that had Mujahedin soldiers?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were, again, rumours, but we could never confirm them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, we are going to end on purely technical questions and I would like you to answer by a 'yes' or "no," please, again, in order to gain time. Is it true that we can consider that there was a railway network, a railway line could be a legitimate military target?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only if you considered a source of locomotion was people pushing the railway cars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have to admit that I did not understand your answer.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You clarified that the Bosnians had no working railway engines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We don't just have testimony in relation to this, however, apart from knowing whether someone was peddling in the locomotive or not, in the engine or not, in theory, would a railway line represent a legitimate target?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the railway line was confirmed as providing logistic support, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, your time is out, so one more minute, but then you have to conclude your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The very last question: Sir, the targets like a network of roads, crossroads, telecommunication centres, official buildings, that were housing command posts and all types of buildings that were housing command posts of any level, are these just listed legitimate military targets?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution objects. That is an extremely compound question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it certainly is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness may answer the question. So let's just split it up. Network of roads?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The majority of support that the Bosnian army would have required them to move people on foot and generally to move supplies on foot. What few vehicles they had were very carefully allocated and used at night when there was very little chance that they would be engaged by direct fire weapons on the Serb side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was rather simple, and whether you could answer that by yes or no, crossroads, could that be a military target?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If there was evidence of military use.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you say it could be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It could be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Telecommunication centres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is a legitimate target, but in the Sarajevo context, they were using Motorolas. It didn't make much sense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Official buildings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Official buildings, again, if they considered they were strongly enough built to have military use --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the question was, official buildings that were housed in command posts and all types of buildings that were housed in command posts, both of any level.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think they are legitimate military targets. But again by the time I arrived there, I would have expected somebody as professional as General Galic to know exactly where these buildings were. If he knew exactly where they were, one of the strategies could have been to destroy the communications or the command structure of the Bosnian army, particularly if there was an attack threatening the Pale road. And I never did understand why the command post --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question is not about what you do understand but whether you would have considered and you have answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for the time given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Mr. Mundis, any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Just a few questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed. Re-examined by Mr. Mundis:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas, you just mentioned and I am quoting: "I would have expected somebody as professional as General Galic to know exactly where these buildings were." What was the basis for your stating that?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I can take a few minutes to elaborate. One of the tactical and operational strategies for a commander in the situation of General Galic is to attack the command structure of the forces that are opposing him. In the case of the Bosnian army, these were very junior officers who had gained their experience at -- gained their knowledge at some expense, combat. Therefore, I think by the time I arrived and General Galic had been in place for over a year, he would know exactly where each command post of each of the Bosnian brigades was. And with the artillery resources at his command, over 209 guns that we knew, he could have systematically attacked those specific headquarters and he had observation, direct observation, on many of them, from the high ground that he controlled. So I think that if he wanted those headquarters destroyed particularly the ones that were attacking towards Pale he could have in fact targeted them and made it a specific artillery target instead of the kind of shelling that took place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas, I would like you to clarify the steps that your UNMOs took in making the distinction between military and civilian victims of sniping?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did you also wish me to talk about artillery victims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will get to that next?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The victims of sniping, the first thing is to try to investigate it in the context of where they were found. If the man is found at a T-junction, and there is no trenches nearby, nothing, you wonder why an individual was killed. If the man is killed near a trench or obviously near a headquarters, then he would be considered a legitimate military target. In those case where the body had been brought to a police station, then we had to rely on the police reporting or reporting of other people. And that is why on the summary you get some asterisks because certainly initially we weren't there in place to see or if somebody else did the investigation, we may not have seen. We could only infer it was probably sniper. Does this answer the question clear enough?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly. With respect to victims of shelling, what steps did your UNMOs take to differentiate between civilian and military victims of shelling?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we said, women and children were automatically considered civilians, although I will admit that one or two women might have been possibly of military service. The men, it was much more difficult, so generally those that we considered not to have been of an age to have done military time in the JNA, they were therefore too young to be much military use and would have required training to be acceptable. Also, there were people over a certain age who would be considered unlikely military personnel which left a large number of young males in an age bracket, I would say, from 17 to certainly 45, depending on how they appeared, which could be considered as possible military age males of soldiers -- or for soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would all of those males in that age group be counted as military for your purposes of reporting?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is where it became a question of context. If the man was walking in the street, for example, the shelling that took place around the new station, where people were walking to avoid Sniper Alley, there was no apparent reason to think they could have been a soldier on leave. It could be anybody. And these might be counted as civilians, those males that fell within the military age. In context, if we could clearly establish that it was in a context; for example, a waiter in a restaurant that was hit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Other than that, however, all males in this age group would be counted as military?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily. As I say, we tried to put it in context. In a lot of cases, we only saw the bodies at the morgue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was other than that

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay, other than that, no. Sorry. Could you rephrase it again just to make sure I am clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Other than the males that you could identify as civilian based on the context, if you could not identify them base on the context, were males in the 17 to 45 year age group counted as military or civilian?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally as military or possibly military.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified earlier that there was increased sniper fire after the ceasefire began to break down?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ye.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if that sniper fire was emanating from both sides or from only one of the sides?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most definitely it came from both sides. And for me, it was an indication of higher direction that we were not satisfied with the ceasefires that we had achieved at the local level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In response to some questions from Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you at least implied that General Galic was of assistance in implementing the ceasefire; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can say that the -- to the best of my knowledge during my time there, during the ceasefire, that no heavy weapons were fired by General Galic's forces. The few investigations that we did of suspected heavy weapons turned out to be hand held antitank weapons fired with a trajectory that was similar to that of a mortar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based on the fact that once the ceasefire came into effect General Galic's forces did not fire any heavy weapons, were you able to draw any conclusions about the command and control structure of the Bosnian Serb army?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I would say that I had much more confidence in the Serbs adhering to their side of the agreement if they agreed, than I did with some of the Bosnian forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that there were rumours of ABiH forces mortaring or shelling Bosnian civilians in the city. To your knowledge, were any investigations carried out to either confirm or deny these rumours?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No investigations were carried out specifically to confirm or deny these rumours. We never had an incident that offered a possibility of doing such an investigation or suggested that it was necessary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In response to some questions with respect to potential discrepancies in the situation reports, I would like to ask you again about observed incoming and outgoing artillery and mortar fire.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any idea or estimate as to what percentage of ingoing or outgoing fire was observed, as a general rule?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within the city, we generally observed incoming fire and so it would be difficult if we were accurate in determining the outgoing fire or the relationship. But I would say, the proportion, there was a lot more incoming than outgoing. The converse was true on the Serb side. We were cited to view outgoing fire and were not in a position to see likely impacts. So the reporting was distorted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time that you were the Senior Military Observer in Sarajevo, did you -- did the UN have any observation posts on Mount Igman?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the observation posts on Mount Igman count or tally outgoing fire from Mount Igman?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we were able to, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, as the witness has mentioned some new information in response to the additional questions asked by the Prosecution, can we in that connection clarify certain points?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Piletta-Zanin, on what issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, can I -- I can say it before the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just see. You understand French, Mr. Thomas?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not well enough to make a response, I don't think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But it is of no use to ask you to take off your headphones because you could still hear Mr. Piletta-Zanin. I will leave it up to you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. If you would just indicate in what -- in respect of what --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Gladly, Mr. President. The answer relates to what was said by the witness in connection with the men who were hit by sniper near a command post. This witness said a while ago, "Yes, we counted that person as a soldier." And we have a very specific question to ask

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just put a question, perhaps not a whole series of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Quite. Further cross-examination by Mr. Piletta-Zanin:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In response to the question asked to you earlier on, you said that if a person, a man of military age carrying weapons were to be found, the victim of a shot near a command post, you would be tempted to consider him a soldier with or without uniform. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This policy applied of course to all members to the best of your knowledge of the UN personnel, at least those that you were in charge of?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This only applied to the United Nations Military Observers who were under my command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. We are talking about the same thing. Witness this does imply that the military observers to be 100 per cent sure would have to know all the command posts all the way up to the company posts. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would not necessarily know the company posts. We would know the battalion command post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But you did not necessarily know the command post of companies nor below that, most probably?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We suspected most of the company command posts were in the front lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But my question was also below the company level.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my army platoon commanders and company commanders are in the front lines

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was not the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: In your army, it may be, sir --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge most company level and lower level officers were in the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question was the following: You told us, Witness, that the UNMO personnel were familiar with the locations of the command post at the level of brigades and battalions; is that what you told us?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Consequently, they were not necessarily familiar with the command posts at the company level and below that level. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there was in fact a command post at that level.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge Nieto-Navia has one or more questions for you. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Well, you said that the UN or at least the military observers considered that they were not prisoners of war but that they were detainees because the Republika Srpska was not considered a legitimate power. My question is whether there was or not a war? I don't mean an international war, but a war.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most definitely there was a war. There was more fire in one day than my colleagues in Afghanistan will see in their entire tour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Okay. Another question is the following: In one of the documents which we have seen number 1753, we can read the following: "The situation within the city is not improving. An aggressive exchange continue between the rival Bosnian and HVO brigades." Could you elaborate a little bit on that?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was -- sorry, did I understand you to say rebel Bosnian --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Rival.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was a fighting between the Bosnian brigades. Two of the Bosnian brigades were commanded by people that I felt had criminal backgrounds. And one of them was eventually -- the commander of the 10th Brigade was eventually disposed of by the Bosnians. So there would be some conflict. In the HVO brigade as well, there was a question that their perception of the front line was that there was criminal activities going on. So in November in Sarajevo, the Bosnian government undertook steps to deal with suspected criminal elements within the Bosnian army. Does that answer your question to enough detail? So without looking at the document, I can't be sure exactly if that is the reference to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: I can give you the date. It is October, 1993.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that would be -- they started what I would call a clean up of criminal activity within the Bosnian army from about the time I arrived until -- it seemed to be finished in November, the end of November.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Of course the document is referring to the HVO.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Croatians were involved in the activities. And we had the anomaly of where the Croatians in Kiseljak shelled the Croatians in Sarajevo who were fighting for the Bosnians. There seemed to be more than met the eye. It was more than fighting than between two belligerents. Of course the position of the HVO in Sarajevo was always tenuous because of course we had both where the HVO was actively fighting the Bosnians. There was some kind of criminal activity. We weren't always --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. Thank you. You mentioned that you saw some tanks activity of the BS army through the city area. I would like you to elaborate a little bit on this issue. I mean, dates if you remember, or areas, which area --

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you talking about the Serb tanks firing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Yes, BSA tanks.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can remember specifically one incident because it is of interest to me as a tanker. I was visiting my OP in Vogosca and from the OP window, about 500 metres away in a field I saw a tank pull up and it was a tank that I was very interested in for professional reasons. It was the Yugoslav army improved version of the T-72. I think it is much the same model as they eventually sold to Kuwait. And this tank not only pulled up into an open field, but it fired. And it fired several rounds. And then it backed off and it disappeared while the team was phoning a complaint to the Vogosca brigade commander. So I went up to the area where this tank had fired and it had -- it seemed to be firing directly down a street. It could not see very much on either side of the street, but with its gun it could cover 3 or 4 kilometres straight down a street. So it was just a very narrow field of fire, but it would control anything that tried to cross the street. I was quite surprised that the tank had been selected to cover this. This is why I made a note. This happened October, November. I remember it was still before the winter. And I remember the incident very well because I was so interested in the tank and also while it fired, the firing characteristics for more than one reason. And then we got up to see it. So this is one specific incident where I saw the tank fire. I don't know the casualties because it would have required relating -- if there would have been casualties, they would have come back in through the city and would been in the morgue, by another team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Do you remember more incidents, more cases?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well of course, on New Years's Eve, the PTT building was hit by a tank round and that was determined by a technical expert that it was a tank round

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Tank round from --

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bosnian Serb tank. So it was -- and that is a technical report which would be available to the Court. And the interesting thing about that was, I was told that it was a Serb tank that fired at another target, but missed the target and it hit us instead. Because I don't think they deliberately targeted the UN building. But the pieces of that round, and there is a technical report available. So that was another direct evidence of tanks firing into the city.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge El Mahdi also has a question for you. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. You said in your testimony that the superior authorities, and now I am referring to the ceasefire, that certain superior authorities did not want the ceasefire to continue. I believe that you said and I shall quote you: [In English] "Not wanting the ceasefire." [Interpretation] Is it an impression you had or did you base this opinion on concrete facts or is it a simple observation or view that you are expressing?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a combination of the three. If I can elaborate on the simple facts. First on the field, the joint commission was to get people from both sides to meet. So in one area, in fact near Rajlovac, which you have already seen on the map, I had the battalion commanders from both sides ready to agree that we would meet in the centre on the line and discuss exactly the position of the front line so that any future violations we would be in agreement as to where the line actually was and what state the trenches were in because that was a complaint, that the lines were being changed or that trenches were being improved or that people retaliated with sniper fire because they were doing work. I had the agreement of both the battalion commanders. I had the agreed time and day and I went down to meet on both sides the teams who were to bring the two commanders up, just the two commanders, and we were to meet at this point. But at the last minute on both sides, there was some reason given they could not do it. That was the example. I knew already from my our discussions with some of the Bosnians that they were afraid or anxious that the ceasefire would put in place a line which would be difficult to change. They thought they would give the Bosnian Serbs territory which did not belong to them, and this line was to be -- would be fixed by a ceasefire. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] So, if I understand correctly, you are saying that the superior authorities, according to you, were targeting mostly the so-called government forces?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that the Bosnians had more reasons not to want the ceasefire than the Serbs. And the reason I say this is, I think -- I think I maybe elaborated last Thursday -- I think the Bosnians were starting to win. That was the first -- for example, in Grbavica. Secondly, they were afraid, and this was again apparent in the negotiations for Gorazde, that they were afraid that the ceasefires would fix the Serb lines and make that the final boundary. So when we talked about the Gorazde ceasefire, they specifically asked that the ceasefire, the Bosnian position, was the ceasefire would only apply to Gorazde and the Serb position was that the ceasefire would apply throughout Bosnia. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] I would like, if you don't mind, to be precise. When you said, "superior authorities" on both sides did Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. you mean or was it on the side of the government forces? That was my question. Your impression.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: My impression was it was on the side -- mainly on the side of the government forces. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] You said also that General Galic actively took part in the implementation of the ceasefire and as a reasoning, you said the shelling stopped and it was only the activities of snipers that continued. Now, do you think that these snipers, did they depend on the superior hierarchy of the Bosnian army or were they a section that was a part, the department that was a part, which was really on the margins of the military hierarchy?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can answer this specifically. In the case of the Bosnians, the only sniper position I visited was under control of the Minister of the Interior. I could not get authority to visit that Bosnian sniper position going through military authorities. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Of the Serb parts?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the Serb side, I had the feeling that it was controlled at the brigade or even battalion level, that there would be instances of sniper fire which appeared to me to be done within a battalion area and had no reference to the overall corps situation. For example, on the Serb side, if there was digging done on the Bosnian side -- and remember the Serbs had fewer people to do the digging, the Bosnian -- the Serbs would respond with sniper fire and then we would intervene by asking them why they were shooting. Then we would take action and then work out a negotiation where the Serbs would stop shooting if the Bosnians would stop digging. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas, I will try to put two questions to you and do it rather quickly because we are quite close to where we have to have break. You testified about that there were rumours that people were killed by people of their own side for, as you said, "other reasons." You were then asked if those be political reasons. You said in some cases, it was "suspected." Then one of the next questions was: "When you spoke of political reasons, would it be perhaps to stir the media or perhaps to increase the figures for political reasons?" You said: "That certainly would be a political reason." Do you know that this reason was applied for, may I say, "intraparty shooting" or was it also in the domain of rumours or...

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can go back to the one example where the man was killed at the T-junction between --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you say, "I know that for this reason, intraparty shooting took place" fine. If you say it is just a deduction or part of rumours, please confirm that.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will say it is a deduction. And my deductions would be based that there was no military reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said sniping increased after the ceasefire. Would that be valid for sniping at military targets or would that be for sniping at civilian targets or both?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to look at that summary. That is one of the reasons we developed that summary, that sniper summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say we could read that from the figures you gave in your summaries?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you could develop -- that is why we did that, to try to analyse it. And there might be casualties there which, again, as I identified earlier, the Serbs did not always report their casualties. There might be other casualties that are not reported.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But that could give us a clue as to the answer to that question. Mr. Thomas -- yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. We have to stop. It is a quarter to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know we have to stop, but perhaps we could recall this witness if you give us leave. This was in relation to the Judge Nieto-Navia regarding the question of the tank that fired and also in to regard to the sniping question which wasn't answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...there, Mr. Thomas, I am not saying good-bye to you at this very moment. We will see whether there are any additional questions for you after the break. We will have a break for one hour and we will start at a quarter to 2.00. And once again I would like to thank the interpreters -- Madam Registrar does not seem to agree. Let's make the break for one hour. That means we will meet back at 10 minutes to 2.00. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.45 p.m. 25

utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin [Interpretation] The Chamber accepts that you may ask another two questions of the witness, that is the last question and the very last question in your language.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President.

Is it true that in your statements you declared two things: The first thing was that Bosniak soldiers were disguised in the tank in some way to -- sorry. I apologise. Serb soldiers were disguised and they were in a tank in order to trick the enemy and you knew about that tank; and the second thing, was that in fact Bosniak soldiers were active with their tanks in the city centre. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is two parts to this question. The first part, are you asking me about the tank that I responded to the Bench about in an earlier statement. There was no question that the Serb soldiers were disguised. The tank was identified as being a Serb tank, it was in the Serb lines and it was in an area known to be occupied by the Serbs. So I don't understand your question when you use the word "disguised". They weren't in the tank in order to trick the enemy because the tank was in obvious view. Again, I don't quite understand how you are framing the question and what you want me to respond. If it was a Bosnian Serb tank that moved into the open after having been camouflaged, fired into the city and then moved back out of site.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said, Witness, the following: [In English] "On the 19th of October 1993, Bosnian soldiers disguised as Serbs shot at the BH Commander. The Bosnians also began to use tanks firing from within the city in what I thought was an attempt to draw retaliatory fire." [Interpretation] Do you recall this in your statement?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You are now talking about not my statement to the Bench, but in fact my testimony that I gave in 1998; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I was talking about your statement, that is it. That is exactly it.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my testimony that I said, yes, indeed, that is a documented allegation that the UN made that in fact the BH Commander in October was fired at by Bosnians who were disguised or simulating Serbs and I suggest that the most appropriate person to question on that is somebody from the BH Command who was in the headquarters at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that is a new issue. It has nothing to do -- well, nothing I don't know. But it is not directly related to the question of the Bench. Please, your last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The very last question, the very last question is in relation to the organisation of snipers. Could you categorically exclude, Witness, that among the snipers, the lone snipers, that these private persons, that they were waging their own private war in some way. Could you exclude the possibility of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't make military sense to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was whether you could exclude that, Mr. Thomas?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not completely, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please finish your answer, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not completely, but it sounds a bit too much like some recent movies. I think that there was no question that sniper activity was directed by the -- in general, by somebody superior to the sniper himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No other questions. Thank you.

utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may ask just a couple of questions to clarify the questions relating to the witness's statement, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I just said that the issue of the witness statement was not in response to the Bench questions. I would rather prevent the parties from going back to the statement which they could have done before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.text: Mr. Thomas, this finally concludes your testimony given in this Court. You have answered the questions of the parties. You have also answered the questions of the Bench. I thank you very much for coming and for staying another weekend here in The Hague. I wish you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Chairman, and if I can in any way add to the proceedings at any time, please feel free.
